HRMS Calc (HRMS Exact Mass Calculator)

← Tools

The electron mass is taken into account. It is subtracted for positive ions and added for negative ions; ignoring it shifts m/z 200 by about 2.7 ppm (more at lower m/z). A survey of about 3000 SI files from Org. Lett. (2023–2024) found errors in about 30% of the reported accurate-mass data; about two-thirds of these came from ignoring the electron mass (Christmann, Org. Lett. 2025, 27, 4⁠–⁠7).

    Everything runs in your browser; nothing you enter is sent anywhere.

    Method

    m/z = (Σ ni mi − z me) / |z|

    ni is the number of atoms in the final ion, mi the isotope mass of each element and z the signed charge. Ions with two or more charges are divided by |z|.

    One electron mass is subtracted per positive charge and added per negative charge (me = 0.0005485799090441 Da).

    Error (ppm) = (measured − calculated) / calculated × 10⁶. Error (mDa) = (measured − calculated) × 1000. The tolerance is applied as a ± range.

    DBE = 1 + C + N/2 − (H + F + Cl + Br + I)/2 (for the neutral M, shown with any fraction). Compositions with elements other than C, H, N, O, S and halogens show —.

    Candidate filters: the DBE condition requires the DBE of the neutral M to be an integer and not negative. DBE is calculated for C, H, N, O, S and halogens with the usual valences (C 4, N 3, H and halogens 1, O and S 2); compositions with other elements are not judged and are kept. Being an integer is the same condition as the nitrogen rule (parity of the number of nitrogens and of the nominal mass); being non-negative is not part of the nitrogen rule (CH6 satisfies the nitrogen rule but has DBE −1). The element-ratio condition uses the ratios of H, N, O, P, S and Si to carbon in the “common range” given by Kind and Fiehn (covering 99.7% of the formulas in their database). Kind & Fiehn, BMC Bioinformatics 2007

    The inputs of the calculator and the formula finder are kept in the page address after “#”. That part is not sent to the server, but a bookmarked or shared address carries the inputs. Inputs of the batch and the checker are not kept in the address.

    84 elements are supported, each with the mass of its most abundant isotope (for example ¹¹B for B and ⁵⁶Fe for Fe). Elements without a natural isotope composition, such as Tc and Pm, cannot be used.

    Isotope patterns are calculated from the NIST abundances; isotopologues with the same nominal mass are combined into one peak (m/z is the abundance-weighted mean). They may be resolved at high resolution.

    The checker takes the formula after “calcd for” as the composition of the ion, recalculates its m/z and checks agreement within rounding of the last digit. Otherwise it looks for errors in the electron mass or a value calculated from the neutral formula.
